articles.title: Centre says tribal leaders are not ‘necessary’ parties to Great Nicobar forest rights dispute
articles.summary: The Union Tribal Affairs Ministry has said that Nicobarese leaders seeking to join a petition challenging the settlement of forest rights on Great Nicobar Island are “neither necessary nor proper parties,” in the case, court documents show. articles.title: Farmers prepare for low rain but get floods instead
articles.summary: “At the Krishi Vigyan Kendra in July, we were told to plant more sesame, groundnut and urad. These are crops expected to withstand less rain. articles.title: The Sundarbans at the crossroads of climate change and human survival [Commentary]
articles.summary: Spanning India and Bangladesh, with India comprising 40% of its area, a vast and ever-shifting mangrove forest stretches across the Bay of Bengal. This vast delta derives its name from the Sundari (Heritiera fomes), the tall mangrove species that flourishes here in abundance. The name “Sundarbans” is a modern rendering of “Sunderbunds,” a term coined […]

articles.title: Community models could help conserve the disappearing migratory freshwater fish [Commentary]
articles.summary: When the United Nations Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS) published its Global Assessment of Migratory Freshwater Fishes report earlier this year, the numbers confirmed what riverine communities had suspected for decades. articles.title: The toxic tyre chemical no one is measuring
articles.summary: Every time a vehicle moves, its tyres shed tiny particles. Some of these particles carry a chemical that, in the U.S., was found killing salmon in urban streams after rain. India is selling more vehicles than ever before, yet experts say there is no data on how much of this chemical reaches the country’s rivers. […]

articles.title: New study maps India’s diverging fire regimes
articles.summary: New research from the Centre for Wildlife Studies evaluated changing fire regimes in wildlife reserves across three Indian landscapes, finding that burned area rose most steeply in the Eastern Ghats between 2002 and 2022, at 9.3% per year. articles.summary: Well past the summer peak, India’s power system remains under strain. The country met daytime demand of over 267 GW even in September, yet fell short by more than 7.7 GW after sunset, when solar generation tapers off. articles.title: New-to-science seahorse is one of three long-misidentified species
articles.summary: Scientists have identified a new-to-science seahorse species from the Indian waters, which has helped resolve the taxonomy of a group misidentified for over a century. articles.title: One orangutan goes home. Will the five babies follow?
articles.summary: Two years since an infant orangutan was seized from a Mumbai apartment, the procedures are finally complete to repatriate him to his homeland, Indonesia. articles.title: Small-scale fisheries a big threat to rays
articles.summary: Manta and devil rays, collectively known as mobulids, are large cartilaginous fish known for their broad, wing-like pectoral fins, which help them glide through the water. articles.summary: A decade ago, Wimarithy K. Marak, a resident of Assam’s Goalpara district, often used to encounter a small pink creature in her neighbourhood’s wells. articles.title: As the Ganga treaty nears expiry, renewed concerns over water sharing arise
articles.summary: As the Ganga water-sharing treaty between India and Bangladesh ends this year, Bihar seeks to resolve its long-standing demands before the treaty is renewed. articles.summary: A recent debate over using DJs and high-powered sound systems during Pune’s Ganesh festival brought noise pollution and its health impacts into focus.
